# Music Assistant — mined review precedents

Project standards distilled from this repository's own past pull-request review discussions; each links the PR where the standard was set. They augment the standards in `AGENTS.md`. Grade against the existing `[CRITICAL]`/`[PROBLEM]`/`[SUGGESTION]` taxonomy in `copilot-instructions.md` — do not restate the output format here. Treat a **MUST** or "won't support" deviation as at least `[PROBLEM]` (a `[CRITICAL]` when it breaks functionality or security); treat a *Prefer* deviation as `[SUGGESTION]`. When you raise one of these, cite its linked PR so the author can see the precedent.

## General standards

Cross-project engineering standards that apply regardless of which repo is in play.

### Architecture & design

- **MUST** keep pull requests small and single-purpose; move unrelated fixes, refactors, or dependency bumps into their own dedicated PR. ([server#2911](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2911#discussion_r2751214136): "This is a bad change slipping in a completely unrelated PR"; [frontend#20](https://github.com/music-assistant/frontend/pull/20#issuecomment-1540353368): "please try to create smaller PR's with only a single change") [mined · 11 PRs · 👍]
- **Prefer** early guard clauses / returns over nested `if`/`else` blocks. ([server#2180](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2180#discussion_r2078576454): "Try using guards to prevent the nested if constructions"; [support#150](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/150#issuecomment-1124984025): "add a guard in the code for this so that it does not completely crash") [mined · 4 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** fix a problem at its root cause and correct owning location, not with a restart/reconnect workaround or a change to a broadly-shared helper with wide blast radius. ([server#2997](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2997#issuecomment-3799464615): "Simply restarting the provider just feels hacky and does not address the root cause"; [server#2341](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2341#issuecomment-3195888556): "This is the wrong location to fix this") [mined · 3 PRs]
- **Prefer** reusing existing shared helpers and extracting duplicated logic into a helper module over reimplementing the same thing per-provider. ([AGENTS.md](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md): "Check `helpers/` for reusable utilities before writing new ones."; [server#3458](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3458#discussion_r3015139669): "We have a ready to use helper available for pls parsing") [authored+mined]
- **Prefer** not introducing an abstraction (helper method, separate file) for logic with only one real consumer; avoid speculative flexibility. ([server#3386](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3386#discussion_r3103034197): "a method with just one call"; [frontend#2073](https://github.com/music-assistant/frontend/pull/2073#discussion_r3564091236): "splitting them into a separate file just adds indirection") [mined · 2 PRs]

### Won't support

- **Won't support** bypassing a provider's ads, DRM, paid tier, or authentication — it violates the provider's ToS, even when technically feasible and done by other unofficial clients. ([server#2463](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2463#issuecomment-3363469430): "we are not going to bypass that, ever"; [server#3388](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3388#issuecomment-4066141033): "We definitely cannot accept this PR as it violates the TOS of Youtube.") [mined · 4 PRs · 👍]
- **Won't support** non-sanctioned deployments and platforms — only officially blessed install methods (HAOS add-on, maintained Docker/containerized images) are supported; bare-metal/custom installs, Kubernetes, and OSes Home Assistant itself doesn't support (FreeBSD/TrueNAS) are out of scope. ([server#2409](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2409#issuecomment-3314742198): "We don't support custom installs of the Music Assistant Server, only our provided"; [support#3630](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/3630#issuecomment-2688879246): "we simply can not support every scenario with our limited team") [mined · 10 PRs]
- **Won't support** AI-generated technical diagnoses or bug reports filed at face value in the tracker; describe problems in your own words. ([support#5201](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5201#issuecomment-4173311388): "Please don't file AI generated reports like this, especially not in an issue tracker."; [support#5334](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5334#issuecomment-4273413814): "AI descriptions of problems are not helpful and are often biased") [mined · 2 PRs]

### Code-quality bar

- **MUST** catch specific, expected exception types — no broad or bare `except`, which hides real bugs. ([server#3096](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3096#discussion_r2768368356): "Broad exceptions are no good. Please identify the specific errors you want to trap"; [server#2332](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2332#discussion_r2322577896): "try to narrow down this exception instead of broadly catching everything") [mined · 11 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** never silently swallow errors or anomalous data — let it propagate or raise; don't collapse failures into a bool, `None`, or a silent default. ([server#1214](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/1214#discussion_r1557137671): "Do not swallow unhandled exceptions, ever."; [server#3722](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3722#discussion_r3106867386): "you are swallowing errors and collapsing them all into a boolean") [mined · 6 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** use `%s`-style positional logging arguments, not f-strings, inside logger calls. ([server#3147](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3147#discussion_r2811140616): "Always use `%s` over `f-string` logging."; [server#1313](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/1313#discussion_r1632251757): "Don't use f-string formatting in log strings") [mined · 3 PRs]
- **MUST** write caller-facing docstrings (what the method does, not its internals); comment only complex blocks and describe current behavior, never change history. ([AGENTS.md](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md): "Only use comments to explain complex, multi-line blocks of code."; [server#3387](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3387#discussion_r3011674453): "A docstring should provide clarity to the caller what the method does") [authored+mined]
- **Prefer** the simplest solution that works; reject overengineered "AI slop" and keep AI-assisted code simple and human-maintainable. ([server#2868](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2868#issuecomment-3707463614): "This seems an overly complex solution for a simple problem"; [server#4919](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4919#issuecomment-5083478791): "Make sure the code remains simple and maintainable") [mined · 4 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** pin third-party GitHub Actions to a verified full commit SHA (Dependabot may still bump them), and design CI security gates to fail closed and resolve identity from trusted API calls. ([support#5911](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/pull/5911#issuecomment-5080017310): "pins the current setup-python release to its verified full SHA"; [server#4618](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4618#discussion_r3529154391): "a failed or partial analysis can never yield a green gate") [mined · 3 PRs]

## Music Assistant standards

MA-domain principles: the provider model, controllers, the streaming pipeline, players, the library, and the API contract.

### Architecture & design

- **MUST** reuse the shared global aiohttp session (`self.mass.http_session`); never create a new `ClientSession` per request or per provider. ([server#1817](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/1817#discussion_r1903244819): "Always re-use the existing global http session and not recreate new ones."; [server#2875](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2875#discussion_r2649564733): "There should already be an http session available to you via `self.mass.http_session`") [mined · 4 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** route external-API lookups through MA's cache (`mass.cache` / `@use_cache`) with a per-method TTL; providers must never hand-roll their own cache layer — even parsed media items go through `mass.cache` / `@use_cache`, while library persistence stays owned by the core controllers. ([server#3640](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3640#discussion_r3072695809): "Please add a 3h cache here to avoid hammering the provider"; [server#586](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/586#discussion_r1150074534): "please do not do any caching in your module, this is all handled") [mined · 8 PRs]
- **MUST** never make a per-item API/DB call inside a loop over a listing (N+1); batch, reuse already-fetched data, or `asyncio.gather` a bounded number of independent calls — never turn an N+1 against a rate-limited provider API into an N-wide burst. ([server#2501](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2501#discussion_r2429740886): "You are fetching the streamdetails for each track in a listing!"; [server#3171](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3171#discussion_r2813508549): "This calls the API for every single track in the list.") [mined · 9 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** keep multi-item listings compact (return `ItemMapping` for nested items); only dedicated get-item endpoints return fully-detailed objects, and library write paths require the real item, never a mapping. ([server#3302](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3302#discussion_r2884140969): "all listings with multiple items are supposed to be compact objects"; [server#2000](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2000#discussion_r1980283283): "In regular (library) listings etc. you can simply return an ItemMapping as album") [mined · 5 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** treat providers as isolated units: never reference another provider by name, reach into another provider or unrelated controller, or touch the database directly — coordinate through the controller API or a generic feature flag. ([server#2502](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2502#discussion_r2428668195): "A provider can only provide its own data, not interact with other providers directly!"; [server#4576](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4576#issuecomment-4886061463): "Providers must never reference each other by name.") [mined · 6 PRs]
- **Won't support** a provider mutating state outside its own domain (player config, another controller); use the official abstraction — a default config value, a provider mapping, the config controller. ([server#2356](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2356#discussion_r2311917075): "We're not going to change a player's config from a source provider.") [mined · 5 PRs]
- **MUST** keep provider-specific quirks inside the provider and shared/player logic in its controller; don't special-case core controllers, extract shared logic to a helper module. ([server#2364](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2364#discussion_r2316187574): "this logic should not be here but in the players controller"; [server#4406](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4406#issuecomment-4783715371): "all you need to fix is the state here within the cast provider") [mined · 3 PRs]
- **MUST** not read or mutate queue/player state directly from a provider; report playback through documented helpers and let the queue controller own the state. ([server#2283](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2283#discussion_r2249779942): "You may not interact with the queue or queue item directly."; [server#2142](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2142#discussion_r2063388238): "you need to tell the queue controller what is playing") [mined · 2 PRs]
- **MUST** keep parsers lightweight, synchronous, and IO-free (raw provider data → MA models); making a parser async or giving it network calls is a hard no. ([server#2472](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2472#discussion_r2400974607): "Parsers should normally be lightweight, IO-free methods that simple take the raw data"; [server#2954](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2954#issuecomment-3738657311): "Parsers should be simple IO-free parsers of (raw) provider specific responses") [mined · 2 PRs]
- **MUST** do auth, setup, and derived-state (base URL) computation in `handle_async_init` / the async setup lifecycle, not `__init__`; MA only exposes the provider after that succeeds and reloads it on every config change. ([server#3836](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3836#discussion_r3575682032): "MA only exposes the provider after `handle_async_init` succeeds."; [server#2008](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2008#discussion_r1986180959): "Is there a reason for doing the setup here instead of in setup ?") [mined · 2 PRs]
- **Prefer** splitting a large provider into `__init__.py`, `constants.py`, `helpers.py`, `provider.py` instead of one big file. ([server#3429](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3429#issuecomment-4095335341): "Please split this into init.py, constants.py, helpers.py and provider.py") [mined · 2 PRs]
- **Prefer** sane defaults over user-facing config options; question whether each toggle is needed and hide genuinely technical ones under `category="advanced"`. ([server#2968](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2968#discussion_r2689490850): "just pick a sane default and get rid of the configuration option"; [server#2228](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2228#discussion_r2149239694): "Why would you want this to be configurable ?") [mined · 9 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** drive all configuration through the UI/config controller; never hand-edit `settings.json` or patch internals when a documented setting already exists. ([server#2928](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2928#discussion_r2683016235): "the settings.json should not be manually touched by either users or developers, ever."; [support#4183](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/4183#issuecomment-3506699722): "There is a player setting to enable/disable that, no need to hack the code.") [mined · 3 PRs]
- **Prefer** gating an expensive/optional provider feature behind a config entry so users can opt out of the extra API/CPU cost. ([server#3110](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3110#issuecomment-4277049207): "Add configentry to enable metadata lookup for radio content") [mined · 2 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** resolve library identity correctly: `item.provider == "library"` means `item_id` is the DB id, `provider_domain='library'` never appears in `provider_mappings`, and you must never treat `mapping.item_id` as a library DB id — resolve it, and prefer an existing library item over a provider API call. ([AGENTS.md](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md): "Never assume you can use `mapping.item_id` directly as a library DB ID"; [server#4804](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4804#discussion_r3582576959): "we should always prefer an existing library item whenever possible") [authored+mined]
- **MUST** keep the library scoped to the user's own curated/favorited items; never silently auto-add — additions always come from an explicit user action. ([server#2339](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2339#discussion_r2449068587): "You should only return in-library or favorited artists here, nothing more, nothing less."; [server#3459](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3459#issuecomment-4150042883): "The basic tenet of MA is we won't add items") [mined · 5 PRs]
- **MUST** process audio internally as raw/float PCM, apply loudness normalization as an EBU R128 integrated-loudness gain (not compression), and only pick the final output codec at the end of the chain based on the target player. ([support#1501](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/1501#issuecomment-1786802167): "All tracks are processed as raw pcm by Music Assistant internally."; [support#3550](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/3550#issuecomment-2642730583): "we only decide at the end of the chain what to actually send") [mined · 2 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** route audio through the streams controller and keep the local streams server LAN-only: plain local-IP HTTP, no HTTPS, reverse proxy, DNS names, or overlay/VPN networks (the separate authenticated webserver/API port, by contrast, may sit behind HTTPS or a reverse proxy). ([server#3976](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3976#issuecomment-4814361185): "The streams server should simply not/never be behind a reverse proxy."; [support#835](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/835#issuecomment-1233185221): "Music Assistant relies on LOCAL NETWORK to stream audio") [mined · 3 PRs]
- **Prefer** native MA player providers (AirPlay, Cast, Sonos, Squeezelite, Sendspin) over generic Home Assistant `media_player` entities — the HA hop breaks reporting/sync and HA players are quirky; use the HA provider only as a last resort. ([support#4507](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/4507#issuecomment-3647684119): "We always recommend to use a native player provider over the Home Assistant Provider"; [support#4573](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/4573#issuecomment-4841890928): "HA media players are known to be quirky and unreliable") [mined · 8 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** expose only a curated, minimal feature set on protocol/virtual players — device-level controls like power belong on the real underlying player, and power integration triggers standby, not a real power-cycle. ([server#4415](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4415#discussion_r3460912727): "A protocol player does not need power."; [support#5777](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5777#issuecomment-4895615880): "no way of distinguishing 'disconnected' or 'powered off' as you literally 'pull the plug'") [mined · 3 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** treat sync/grouping as a virtual layer over players sharing native protocol-level sync — players on different protocols or Universal groups can't sync; apply group volume so members keep their relative balance (the controller interpolates toward the target rather than setting every member to the same absolute level), and route group/sync commands through the sync leader. ([support#4422](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/4422#issuecomment-3577606442): "Universal groups do not support sync."; [server#867](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/867#issuecomment-1782825267): "each individual player should be increased with 30%, regardless of its current value") [mined · 6 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** stay event-driven: when state looks stale, add or fix the missing event instead of polling; prefer mDNS/announcement discovery, and poll hardware adaptively only when actively playing. ([server#2810](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2810#discussion_r2620775575): "everything is event driven. So if we are missing an event somewhere"; [support#2819](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/2819#issuecomment-2433372037): "we rely purely on mdns announcements") [mined · 3 PRs · 👍]
- **Prefer** the built-in scheduler/debouncer (`mass.call_later`, with a `task_id` for debouncing) and the player controller's wait helpers (`wait_for_player_update`) over hand-rolled timers, sleep loops, or arbitrary `sleep` guesses. ([server#3020](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3020#discussion_r3102897247): "we have a task scheduler for this - please adjust the logic"; [server#2758](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2758#discussion_r2594785911): "Better use the wait_for_state helper within the player controller to actually wait") [mined · 5 PRs]
- **MUST** keep `StreamDetails` audio-quality fields (codec, bit depth, sample rate) accurate since they drive playback — set `ContentType.UNKNOWN` rather than guess wrong; regular item metadata may be approximate, and sample rate/bit depth only matter for raw/non-container formats. ([server#626](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/626#discussion_r1168251023): "For the streamdetails these details NEED to be accurate, for just the regular"; [server#2295](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2295#discussion_r2262410742): "You can skip the sample rate and bit depth - that is only important") [mined · 2 PRs]
- **MUST** bump `API_SCHEMA_VERSION` for a backwards-incompatible client-facing addition — a new or changed API command, a shared-model change, or a new remote-access gateway channel label (an older server mistakes an unknown label for the API channel and breaks the whole session) — so that the clients that are not bundled with the server (the Home Assistant integration, the companion apps, third-party API consumers) can gate on the server's `schema_version`. The frontend ships in lockstep with the server and never gates on `schema_version`, so never ask for a frontend gate. Additions that stay backwards-compatible for existing clients — an ordinary raw HTTP route, or an opt-in `PROVIDER_EVENT` subscription older clients simply ignore — do not need a bump; nor does a bug fix or behavior change that leaves a command's signature, parameters, and return shape unchanged, since a client cannot and need not feature-detect it. ([server#4487](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4487#discussion_r3634100959): "please also bump API_SCHEMA_VERSION - we add a new api command here"; Marcel: "the frontend is always shipped in lockstep with the backend - it NEVER needs schema gating"; [webserver README](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/HEAD/music_assistant/controllers/webserver/README.md): "Bump `API_SCHEMA_VERSION` ... when adding a label and gate the client on the new value") [authored+mined]
- **Won't support** implementing a cross-client feature in one client — anything affecting frontend, mobile, and HA belongs in the backend/server so every client benefits. ([frontend#1569](https://github.com/music-assistant/frontend/pull/1569#issuecomment-4106241960): "do this completely in the backend so it works with ALL api clients") [mined · 1 PR]

### Won't support

- **Won't support** free/basic streaming accounts (e.g. Spotify Free, YouTube Music free) — a paid/premium account is required, and free-tier playback of paid services is a legal non-starter. ([support#481](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/481#issuecomment-1180548863): "Free Spotify accounts are not supported."; [support#2487](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/2487#issuecomment-2175235442): "We have never (and will never) support PAID music services for free.") [mined · 4 PRs]
- **Won't support** replicating features Home Assistant core already provides — MA stays a music-focused app, not a general HA-feature clone (media-server *music* libraries — Plex, Emby, Jellyfin, Subsonic — are supported, via dedicated providers). ([support#112](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/112#issuecomment-1126029764): "I do not want to replicate features that are already in HA") [mined · 1 PR]
- **Won't support** cloning LMS quirk-for-quirk or chasing end-of-life hardware — implement the protocol in its clean base form and support only the reference client (e.g. squeezelite). ([support#1490](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/1490#issuecomment-2011834530): "I have zero intention to turn MA into a LMS clone."; [support#2633](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/2633#issuecomment-2708841956): "We will only support squeezelite based players from now on") [mined · 3 PRs]
- **Won't support** fully fixing every quirk of notoriously flaky protocols (DLNA) — best-effort only, and prefer a better-specified protocol (AirPlay) when a device offers both. ([support#1315](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/1315#issuecomment-1589597974): "DLNA is a flaky protocol, implemented in 99999 different ways on devices."; [support#2514](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/2514#issuecomment-2436510301): "DLNA is the crappiest protocol on earth.") [mined · 3 PRs]
- **Won't support** multi-channel/surround audio (e.g. Dolby Atmos) — the pipeline is stereo-only since no supported player target consumes multi-channel. ([support#1961](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/1961#issuecomment-2004616191): "We wont be able to process that anyway, we only do stereo.") [mined · 1 PR]
- **Won't support** letting users run resource-heavy optional features (audio analysis, smart fades) on underpowered hardware — they're gated behind minimum requirements, and the gate can't be overridden because playback would be at risk. ([support#5633](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5633#issuecomment-4705682915): "shields memory-extensive features (such as audio analysis) behind a minimum memory requirement"; [support#5673](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5673#issuecomment-4749531877): "worst of all, playback will be affected. That is too much of a risk.") [mined · 3 PRs · 👍]
- **Won't support** playback scope creep — playback needs a device that accepts a direct stream URL ("play from url"), and MA tracks only its own playback, not state from other software controlling the same player. ([support#101](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/101#issuecomment-1158188280): "it is required that the enddevice (the speaker) supports \"play from url\""; [support#1129](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/1129#issuecomment-1464970040): "MA only tracks its own playback to players and ignores other playback.") [mined · 2 PRs]

### Code-quality bar

- **MUST** raise from MA's own typed exception hierarchy (`MediaNotFoundError`, `LoginFailed`, `SetupFailedError`, `ProviderUnavailableError`, …), chaining with `raise ... from err`; never return `None` as a not-found/error signal. ([server#1982](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/1982#discussion_r1974013590): "you need to raise a MediaNotFoundError here and not return None, that will"; [server#3900](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3900#discussion_r3255835790): "Should be UnsupportedFeaturedException from MA errors, not the Python built-in") [mined · 6 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** validate any user-configured filesystem path against traversal (via `helpers/security.py > is_safe_path`) before file operations. ([server#3276](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3276#discussion_r2912220089): "We have a helper for path validation under helpers/security.py > is_safe_path") [mined · 2 PRs]
- **MUST** handle secrets carefully: decrypt before any outbound third-party call, mask secure config values in serialization, persist rotated tokens immediately (not via a debounced save), and never write credentials to logs. ([server#4882](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4882#discussion_r3634243924): "ConfigEntry serialization does not mask secure strings"; [support#2583](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/2583#issuecomment-2213501294): "hide the password from logging") [mined · 3 PRs]
- **MUST** pin exact versions for provider-specific dependencies, and keep a plugin-only dependency in that plugin's own manifest. ([support#2054](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/2054#issuecomment-2016621794): "we should always use pinned versions in the provider requirements, especially for these"; [server#4912](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4912#discussion_r3648949024): "this dependency is only used for the party plugin") [mined · 3 PRs]
- **MUST** not hardcode a limit a real user can exceed (e.g. a fixed library-size cap); paginate or derive the value instead. ([server#3640](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3640#discussion_r3072722851): "What if a user's library is larger than 2000?"; [server#3722](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3722#discussion_r3111722897): "It would be more future proof if you didnt hard code here?") [mined · 2 PRs · 👍]

## Per-project notes

### server (`music-assistant/server`)

Python/asyncio backend. The heaviest-mined repo; most of the Overall and MA rules above are evidenced here. Repo-specific mechanics:

- **MUST** run the container in host (or bridge) networking for mDNS discovery; SMB/CIFS mounting additionally needs the root user plus the `SYS_ADMIN`/`DAC_READ_SEARCH` capabilities (full privileged mode is a superset that also works). ([support#1332](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/1332#issuecomment-1609297129): "the MA container must run in host networking mode (or bridge"; [support#2956](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/2956#issuecomment-2382542643): "you don't need privileged at all. You only need the 'sys_admin' and 'dac_read_search' if you want to mount filesystems") [mined · 3 PRs]
- **MUST** run `pre-commit run --all-files` after a change / before pushing so CI doesn't fail on avoidable lint/mypy errors. ([AGENTS.md](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md): "Always run `pre-commit run --all-files` after a code change"; [server#4197](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4197#issuecomment-4698242341): "Make sure you always run pre-commit before pushing.") [authored+mined]
- **MUST** only mark a review comment resolved after fixing the code or explaining why it doesn't apply. ([server#4217](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4217#issuecomment-4741516130): "Only resolve comments if you adjusted the code and fixed the review comment") [mined · 2 PRs]
- **MUST** not depend on Python set ordering — sort explicitly for serialization/snapshot tests, and give listing/pagination queries a deterministic sort with a stable default. ([server#1485](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/1485#issuecomment-2218106483): "the order will be random and the test will simply fail sometimes"; [server#4806](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4806#discussion_r3634349239): "leaves the union completely unordered, which also makes limit/offset pagination non-deterministic") [mined · 2 PRs · 👍]
- **MUST** manage background asyncio tasks: keep a reference to `create_task`, track and cancel them on unload, run teardown in a `finally`, and give them a done-callback so failures surface. ([server#3492](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3492#discussion_r3051739796): "any exceptions raised by that task are silently lost with no way to know"; [server#4879](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4879#discussion_r3622539212): "teardown now runs in `finally`, so a failed STOP write can") [mined · 4 PRs]
- **MUST** explicitly clean up related/child rows on delete — the DB has no cascade delete enabled. ([server#3327](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3327#discussion_r2905335902): "We don't have cascade delete enabled for the DB so you'd need to cleanup") [mined · 1 PR]

**Stored data & migrations** — config entries (`settings.json`) and library/cache/auth database rows are live user data; changing their shape only breaks the installs that already hold data. `AGENTS.md` sets the baseline (ask before deciding; make a step idempotent, tolerant of half-written values, and never raising); these are the review precedents on top of it:

- **MUST** ship a migration when a change alters data existing installs already hold — a stored provider item id, a config key or its type, where a value lives — instead of silently switching and orphaning the old rows or keys, unless one of the no-migration cases below applies (it cannot be done faithfully, the affected installs recover on their own, or only an entry's default changed). ([server#5180](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/5180#discussion_r3895354313): "that is a change to stored user data and the old rows are orphaned"; [server#3870](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3870#discussion_r3766494711): "Do we need a migration for this?"; [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md): "Config entries and database rows are live user data.") [authored+mined]
- **MUST** clear or convert legacy stored config keys in a core migration step (`controllers/config/migrations.py`), not in the provider or its setup flow — that code only runs when someone reruns setup, so everyone else keeps the stale value; and once a core step removes a key, provider-side checks for it are dead code. ([server#5589](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/5589#discussion_r4175696071): "belongs in a config migration, not the setup form, because this code only runs when someone reruns setup"; [server#5589](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/5589#discussion_r4175662425): "a user who never reruns setup keeps an unused x_token stored forever") [mined · 1 PR]
- **Prefer** a one-off step in the existing migrations module over a separate migration module or legacy-format handling inside the new code. ([server#6377](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6377#discussion_r4187349427): "Can't we just do a once-off migration in music/migrations.py and keep the 'legacy knowledge' out of the new solution?") [mined · 1 PR]
- **MUST** treat everything a migration step reads as unvalidated — it runs against the raw settings file or raw rows, before any model validation — so type-check values and skip what it can't handle rather than raising; a failed library migration resets the database. ([server#6622](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6622#discussion_r4153896975): "a failed migration costs a full rescan. Non-text metadata and image paths are now skipped instead of raising"; [server#5525](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/5525#issuecomment-5231295104): "The defensive checks elsewhere are in the migrations, which run against the raw file before it is validated."; [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/HEAD/AGENTS.md): "let it survive missing and half-written values, and never let it raise") [authored+mined]
- **MUST** fail closed when a migration step can't convert a record that governs access or visibility — write the most restrictive state rather than leaving it open. ([server#6255](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6255#discussion_r3982066484): "a source whose conversion fails is now written as private (hidden until an admin sets its access) instead of staying open") [mined · 1 PR]
- **MUST** respect ordering between migrations: a step may only rely on data an earlier-running migration has already written — the library database migrates during music-controller setup, before later startup migrations such as provider access — so park the dependent part and settle it once that data exists. ([server#6482](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6482#discussion_r4113538618): "The migration only parks every favorite under the placeholder user; settle_pending() runs right after migrate_provider_access() and does the attribution with the owners known.") [mined · 1 PR]
- **MUST** carry references along when a migration renames, merges, or collapses an identifier — whatever still points at the old id (user provider filters, links) maps to the survivor instead of being pruned away. ([server#6026](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6026#discussion_r3865027795): "filter entries naming a collapsed instance now map to the surviving instance (map-before-keep in the auth prune), with a test") [mined · 1 PR]
- **MUST** match exactly the legacy data a migration owns: cover every state earlier versions could have left behind, but don't sweep up rows or configs another provider wrote — a prefix or path fragment alone is too weak. ([server#6622](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6622#discussion_r4153991629): "it should match the playlist rows anyway. Now also requires the builtin provider"; [server#5525](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/5525#discussion_r3743632273): "Widened the migration: a disabled protocol config is now dropped when neither side of the link survives"; [server#5559](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/5559#issuecomment-5247912762): "the prefix alone could be too weak since providers are free to choose their own id formats") [mined · 3 PRs]
- **Prefer** narrowing a data migration in SQL so only the affected rows are loaded — it runs at startup against the whole library. ([server#6715](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6715#discussion_r4183878803): "so only rows with an empty image path get loaded") [mined · 1 PR]
- **MUST** test a migration against the stored shape of the old version, in the core migration tests under `tests/controllers/` (such as `music/test_music_migrations.py` and `config/test_migrations.py`, or the migration's own module beside them) — don't copy core migration tests into a provider's test folder. ([server#5585](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/5585#discussion_r3891197342): "add the domain to the existing test in the core file rather than keeping a copy here"; [server#6255](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6255#discussion_r3981948947): "the migration tests run against stored configs carrying the plain string and convert them") [mined · 2 PRs]
- **MUST** tag each settings migration step with the release after which it can be deleted (`# TODO: remove after 2.NN release`), choosing the nearest sensible release rather than a distant one; expired steps are pruned. ([server#5167](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/5167#discussion_r3712632224): "Why not 2.10?"; [server#5167](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/5167#pullrequestreview-4833726175): "The migration until 2.13 might be a little long from what I have seen before"; [server#6221](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6221): "Remove settings migrations that were due to go after 2.9") [mined · 2 PRs]
- **Won't support** backporting a data migration to `stable`; it waits for the next release. ([server#6715](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6715#issuecomment-6010795110): "not backporting since it's a data migration, leaving it for 2.11") [mined · 1 PR]
- **Prefer** no migration over an unfaithful one: skip a backfill that would have to guess or fabricate values, or where affected installs recover on the next sync or re-pair — and state that trade-off in the PR description. ([server#6188](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6188#discussion_r3923461110): "A backfill cannot be done faithfully"; [server#6026](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/6026#discussion_r3865072202): "Deliberate trade-off (noted in the description)") [mined · 2 PRs]

---

## Avoid these false positives

Patterns that look like bugs but are correct here — do not raise them:

- **A walrus-bound name is bound once its expression runs.** A name assigned with `:=` is bound as soon as that walrus expression evaluates — even if the surrounding condition is then False — so do not report `UnboundLocalError` / "used before assignment" for it there. Only flag it when the walrus itself may be skipped (e.g. it sits on the short-circuited side of `or`/`and`).
- **A quoted type in `cast()` does not make its import unused.** `cast("SomeType", x)` with the type as a string is ruff's `TC006` form; ruff and mypy resolve names inside quoted casts, so the import is used. Do not flag it as an unused import.
- **No `await`, no race.** Do not report a TOCTOU / check-then-act race unless there is a real suspension point (`await`) between the check and the mutation. Single-threaded asyncio runs code with no `await` between them atomically, so nothing can interleave.
- **`except A, B:` without parentheses is valid Python 3.14 (PEP 758).** Catching multiple exception types without parentheses — `except MediaNotFoundError, AudioError:` (and `except* A, B:`) — is standard syntax as of Python 3.14 (PEP 758), which this repo targets (`requires-python >= 3.14`). It is NOT the removed Python-2 `except E, name:` binding form and is NOT a syntax error; do not flag it or suggest adding parentheses. Parentheses remain required only when an `as` clause is present: `except (A, B) as e:`.
- **Valid modern Python is not a syntax error — the target is 3.14.** `pyproject.toml` pins `requires-python >= 3.14`, and CI runs that interpreter plus ruff and mypy, so anything that would not parse is already red in CI. Do not report recent-but-valid syntax as invalid: PEP 695 `type X = ...` aliases and `def f[T](...)` type parameters (3.12), PEP 701 nested f-strings (3.12), and PEP 758 parenthesis-less `except` (3.14, above).
- **`except Exception` around a duplicate-column check is the migration idiom.** In `controllers/music/migrations.py` an `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` step catches `Exception` and re-raises unless the message contains `duplicate column` — that is what makes the step safe to re-run, and it is the prevailing idiom in that file. Do not flag it as a broad except or ask one step to switch to `sqlite3.OperationalError`; narrowing them is a separate file-wide cleanup.
- **A changed config-entry default needs no migration.** Config only persists values that differ from the entry's default (`Config.to_raw()`), so installs that never changed the setting simply pick up the new default, and a value the user did change must be left alone. Do not ask for a migration that rewrites the old default.
